answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit work, and the protocol slashes that stake when independent audits show it is fabricating results or colluding. Creating a hundred fake identities no longer gives an attacker influence for free: every identity needs its own capital at risk, which honest participants can seize through verified challenges. A comet of new accounts may brighten the nebula, but without costly deposits it cannot steer rewards; saffron-colored profile details change nothing.
